annarbor-ward-boundary.summary: Ann Arbor elects two council members from each of five wards, and this app does not show you which ward you live in.
annarbor-ward-boundary.why: The only copy of the ward map this app can read automatically is an older plan that no longer matches the state's current precincts, and the city's own data portal needs a browser to search.
annarbor-ward-boundary.wanted: The city's current ward boundary as a downloadable file or a public map service, from the city's own data portal.

bay-city-ward-boundary.summary: Bay City elects nine commissioners by ward, and this app does not show you which ward you live in.
bay-city-ward-boundary.why: The city's published ward map and the state's current precinct map disagree about where several ward lines run, so showing either one would risk telling you the wrong ward.
bay-city-ward-boundary.wanted: Bay City's current adopted ward boundary, republished so it agrees with the precincts the state records for the city.

bedford-township-board.summary: In Bedford township the Township or City card names the township but not its board.
bedford-township-board.why: The robots.txt served at the township's own address asks automated visitors to stay out, and this project honours that.
bedford-township-board.wanted: The township board list from a source the township allows, or its permission to read the board page.

burton-council-roster.summary: In Burton the City or Village card names the city but not its council.
burton-council-roster.why: The city's website answers this app with a Cloudflare challenge page, which is an access control, and this project does not work around one.
burton-council-roster.wanted: The council roster from a source this app can read, or a word from the city on whether the challenge is meant for a site like this one.

dearborn-council-form.summary: Dearborn has no council district card here, because it is not settled that it elects its council by district at all.
dearborn-council-form.why: The state records no ward number for any Dearborn precinct, where it records them for every other Michigan city this app covers, which points to a council elected by the whole city rather than by ward.
dearborn-council-form.wanted: The city charter's own words on how the council is elected, or a certified county canvass showing the council contest and how many seats each voter fills.

detroit-council-contact.summary: In Detroit the City Council District card names your council member and the two elected citywide, and gives you the Council's main office — but no way to reach that member directly.
detroit-council-contact.why: Detroit publishes one phone number for the whole Council and none for any individual member, so this app shows you the Council's own office and links the member's page rather than inventing a direct line.
detroit-council-contact.wanted: A phone number or e-mail per council member on the city's own council pages, so the card can reach the member it already names rather than only the Council's main line.

holland-mi-ward-boundary.summary: Holland is not among the Michigan cities whose council wards this app can draw.
holland-mi-ward-boundary.why: Neither the city nor its county publishes a ward boundary in any form this app could read.
holland-mi-ward-boundary.wanted: Holland's six ward boundaries as a service or a downloadable file.

kentwood-ward-boundary.summary: Kentwood is not among the Michigan cities whose council wards this app can draw.
kentwood-ward-boundary.why: Neither the city nor its county publishes a ward boundary in any form this app could read.
kentwood-ward-boundary.wanted: Kentwood's two ward boundaries as a service or a downloadable file.

lansing-ward-boundary.summary: Lansing elects four of its eight council members by ward, and this app does not show you which ward you live in.
lansing-ward-boundary.why: The city publishes its ward map on terms that bar commercial use. That is a condition on the map rather than a technical block, and it has not been resolved instead of being worked around.
lansing-ward-boundary.wanted: Permission to use the city's ward map on a free public site, or the same boundary published on open terms.

mi-commissioner-roster.summary: All 83 Michigan counties now name a commissioner on the district card. In 52 the name is read from the county's own board page each week; in the other 31 it is the winner the state certified in November 2024, and the card says so.
mi-commissioner-roster.why: No county among those 31 publishes a list this app can read, so the only source covering them is the state's record of who won the last election. That is true on its own terms and will still name someone who has since left.
mi-commissioner-roster.wanted: For each of the 31: a board page an automated reader may see, so the card can name who holds the seat now. For Monroe District 2, Lenawee District 5, Ionia District 3 and Clinton District 4: a county page naming the seat.

mi-county-board-access-controlled.area: Allegan County, Branch County, Gladwin County, Iosco County, Livingston County, Oakland County and Ottawa County, Michigan
mi-county-board-access-controlled.summary: Allegan, Branch, Gladwin, Iosco, Livingston, Oakland and Ottawa counties' websites refuse or challenge automated visitors, so their cards name the winners of the last certified election instead of who holds the seat now.
mi-county-board-access-controlled.why: Some of these sites answer a challenge page instead of a document, and the rest refuse this app at their edge — the same refusal an ordinary browser gets, so there is nothing to change on our side.
mi-county-board-access-controlled.wanted: A page listing each county's commissioners by district that automated visitors are allowed to reach.

mi-county-board-no-district-key.area: Alger County, Antrim County, Bay County, Benzie County, Crawford County, Mason County, Mecosta County and St. Joseph County, Michigan
mi-county-board-no-district-key.summary: Alger, Antrim, Bay, Benzie, Crawford, Mason, Mecosta and St. Joseph counties publish their commissioners without saying which district each one represents.
mi-county-board-no-district-key.why: This app answers by district, and their board pages name people with no district beside the name, so a name could not be put on the right seat without guessing.
mi-county-board-no-district-key.wanted: The district number beside each commissioner's name, on the page the county already publishes.

mi-county-board-page-names-nobody.summary: Montmorency County's board page names no commissioner at all, so its card names the winners of the last certified election instead of who holds the seat now.
mi-county-board-page-names-nobody.why: The page the county links for its board is all menu and no content, and a separate page its menu names has not been read, so nothing this app has seen lists the members.
mi-county-board-page-names-nobody.wanted: The page where the county lists its commissioners by district.

mi-county-board-page-not-found.area: Baraga County, Charlevoix County, Huron County, Iron County, Missaukee County and Wexford County, Michigan
mi-county-board-page-not-found.summary: Baraga, Charlevoix, Huron, Iron, Missaukee and Wexford counties have readable websites, but not a board page this app could find at any address it has tried.
mi-county-board-page-not-found.why: Their sites answer, and neither the site map nor the front page links a page listing the commissioners. Four counties once in this record turned out to publish one at a second address, so this is about the addresses tried.
mi-county-board-page-not-found.wanted: A link to the page where each county lists its commissioners by district.

mi-county-board-prose-roster.area: Manistee County, Newaygo County, Van Buren County and Washtenaw County, Michigan
mi-county-board-prose-roster.summary: Manistee, Newaygo, Van Buren and Washtenaw counties name their commissioners only inside written biographies, which this app cannot read reliably enough to use.
mi-county-board-prose-roster.why: The names sit in running prose rather than a list, in several different sentence shapes, and one district's biography does not begin with the name at all, so a parser would put some names on the wrong seat.
mi-county-board-prose-roster.wanted: The commissioners listed by district, as a list rather than inside biographies.

mi-county-board-robots-declined.area: Genesee County, Gogebic County, Ingham County, Marquette County and Tuscola County, Michigan
mi-county-board-robots-declined.summary: Genesee, Gogebic, Ingham, Marquette and Tuscola counties ask automated tools not to read their websites, so their cards name the winners of the last certified election instead of who holds the seat now.
mi-county-board-robots-declined.why: Each county's own robots file tells automated tools not to read the site, and this project honours that. The districts still draw, and the map still tells you which one you are in.
mi-county-board-robots-declined.wanted: Permission to read the board page, or the same roster published somewhere the county's own rules allow.

mi-isd-board-members.summary: The Intermediate School District card names your district and says how its board is chosen, but not who sits on it.
mi-isd-board-members.why: In most of these districts the board is picked by the local school boards rather than by voters, and nothing gathers the members of all 56 boards into one list.
mi-isd-board-members.wanted: A district-by-district roster from each intermediate school district's own board page, refreshed weekly.

mi-judge-roster.area: Michigan — the Court of Appeals' 4 districts and all 57 circuits
mi-judge-roster.summary: The Court of Appeals and Circuit Court cards name your district and circuit but not the judges elected there.
mi-judge-roster.why: The state court system's website lists every judge, and it asks automated tools not to read any of it. The other published list is the Michigan Manual, which is printed once every two years and would go out of date between editions.
mi-judge-roster.wanted: A list of sitting judges by circuit and Court of Appeals district that the state court system lets automated tools read, or its permission to read the one it already publishes.

mi-municipal-officeholders.area: Michigan — every city and village below 25,000 people, and five cities above it
mi-municipal-officeholders.summary: The City or Village card names the council of 39 of Michigan's largest cities, read weekly from their own websites; four more are named on the council district card. Other cities and villages are named without their officials.
mi-municipal-officeholders.why: Each city and village publishes its own officials and nothing gathers them into one list, so each council is read from its own city's site. That is done for the large cities; the rest are named without people rather than guessed.
mi-municipal-officeholders.wanted: For Rochester Hills, Norton Shores and Burton: permission to read the council page, or a list this app can read. For Dearborn Heights: a re-read after the 13 October 2026 appointment. For the rest: a roster per municipality.

mi-school-board-members.summary: Both School District cards name your district but not its elected board — no statewide roster of Michigan school board members exists.
mi-school-board-members.why: Michigan school boards are elected, and the district boundaries this app draws come from the Census, which records geography and no people at all.
mi-school-board-members.wanted: A statewide board roster from the department or the association, or a district-by-district build refreshed weekly, the way this project names officeholders everywhere else.

mi-township-officers.area: Michigan — every township below 25,000 people, and two above it
mi-township-officers.summary: The Township or City card names the board of 32 of Michigan's largest townships, read weekly from their own websites. For every other township it names the township but not its board: no statewide list of township officers exists.
mi-township-officers.why: Each township elects its own board and nobody publishes them as one list, so each board is read from its own township's site. That is done for the large townships; for the rest the card names the office rather than guessing who holds it.
mi-township-officers.wanted: For West Bloomfield and Bedford: permission to read the board page, or a copy of the board list. For the rest: a statewide roster from the state or the townships association.

mi-tribal-government.summary: The Tribal Government card names the council of nine of Michigan's twelve nations, from each nation's own page. It names nobody for Hannahville, Keweenaw Bay or Little River.
mi-tribal-government.why: Two of those sites sit behind a check only a person in a browser can pass, which this project does not get around. Little River shows its council to members only. Michigan has no current state list.
mi-tribal-government.wanted: A council list from Hannahville, Keweenaw Bay and Little River that this project may read, or a current state list naming them.

midland-ward-boundary.summary: Midland is not among the Michigan cities whose council wards this app can draw.
midland-ward-boundary.why: Neither the city nor its county publishes a ward boundary; the only district column on offer belongs to the county board, not the city council.
midland-ward-boundary.wanted: The city's five ward boundaries as a service or a downloadable file.

muskegon-ward-boundary.summary: Muskegon is not among the Michigan cities whose council wards this app can draw.
muskegon-ward-boundary.why: The only ward map published for the city leaves parts of the city itself uncovered, so it cannot answer for every address inside it.
muskegon-ward-boundary.wanted: A ward boundary that covers the whole city, published by the city or the county. The state's precinct map may only be used to check a city's ward boundary here, not to stand in for one.

norton-shores-council-roster.summary: In Norton Shores the City or Village card names the city but not its council.
norton-shores-council-roster.why: The city's robots.txt asks automated visitors not to read its website, and this project honours that.
norton-shores-council-roster.wanted: The council roster from a source the city allows, or the city's permission to read its council page.

pontiac-ward-boundary.summary: Pontiac elects its council by district, and this app does not show you which district you live in.
pontiac-ward-boundary.why: What the city publishes is a precinct map from 2020 rather than a district map, and it no longer matches the precincts the state records for the city.
pontiac-ward-boundary.wanted: Pontiac's current council-district boundary as a downloadable file or a public map service.

rochester-hills-council-roster.summary: In Rochester Hills the City Council District card names your district but not your council member.
rochester-hills-council-roster.why: The city publishes a maintained council page naming all seven members with a phone and an e-mail each, and its robots.txt asks automated visitors not to read the site.
rochester-hills-council-roster.wanted: The council roster from a source the city has not asked crawlers to leave alone — an open-data endpoint, a published feed, or the city's own permission.

sterling-heights-council-form.summary: Sterling Heights is one of Michigan's largest cities and has no council district card here, because it is not yet settled whether it elects its council by district at all.
sterling-heights-council-form.why: Four separate signals all point to a council elected by the whole city, which would mean there is no district to show. None of them is the city or the county saying so outright, so nothing is claimed either way.
sterling-heights-council-form.wanted: The city charter's own words on how the council is elected, or a certified county canvass showing the council contest and how many seats each voter fills.

west-bloomfield-township-board.summary: In West Bloomfield the Township or City card names the township but not its board.
west-bloomfield-township-board.why: The robots.txt served at the township's own address asks automated visitors to stay out, and this project honours that.
west-bloomfield-township-board.wanted: The township board list from a source the township allows, or its permission to read the board page.

wyoming-mi-council-roster.summary: In Wyoming the City or Village card names the city but not its council.
wyoming-mi-council-roster.why: The operator has ruled that this project does not read the city's website, so its council page is not read.
wyoming-mi-council-roster.wanted: The council roster from a source outside the city's website, or a decision by the operator to write to the city.

wyoming-mi-ward-boundary.summary: Wyoming elects its council by ward, and this app does not show you which ward you live in.
wyoming-mi-ward-boundary.why: The city asks automated tools not to read the part of its website where its ward and precinct maps are published, and this project honours that.
wyoming-mi-ward-boundary.wanted: Wyoming's three ward boundaries as a downloadable file or a map service, from the city outside the closed part of its site, from its county, or from the regional GIS agency it uses.
